<main class="site-main"><section class="page-intro"><p class="section-number">Article · Models and meaning</p><h1>Real Vs. Fake news in football</h1><div class="article-meta"><span class="status">in bloom</span><span>12 May 2023</span></div></section><article class="prose"><p>Can the language of a football story give away whether it is real or fake? This experiment uses text classification to ask a question that is more difficult than the title makes it sound.</p><h2>The setup</h2><p>Text becomes features. Features become a classifier. The classifier becomes a chance to inspect what language patterns it can use, and where it is likely to learn the dataset instead of the claim.</p><h2>The useful caution</h2><p>A high score on a held-out split is not automatically evidence that a model understands truth. Source, style, repetition, and leakage can all masquerade as meaning.</p><p>NLP, but of the good kind: small enough to inspect.</p></article></main>
